title: Pineapple-centre square
subtitle: A square motif with a lace pineapple panel worked into the centre rounds
excerpt: A pineapple motif grows from the magic ring and fills the centre of the square, its graduated treble fans pointing outward from the magic ring. The outer rounds close the pineapple into a square with standard corner clusters. The pineapple read is strongest in a single colour against a plain background yarn.
sourceNotes: Pineapple crochet is a classic American and Victorian motif documented extensively in Weldon's Practical Needlework, Volume 7 (1892), and in early American thread-crochet booklets from the 1890s.
heroPrompt: A pineapple-centre crochet square in fine white cotton thread on a pale linen background, photographed flat from above in soft daylight. Lace pineapple pattern visible in the centre, square border with chain-2 corners, 12 cm across.

crochet.gaugeText: Finished pineapple-centre square measures 12 × 12 cm in 4-ply cotton thread with a 2.5 mm hook.

chartDefinition.title: Pineapple-centre square
chartDefinition.caption: Rounds 1–5 build the pineapple fans from the magic ring. Rounds 6–7 close into a square with chain-2 corners.

glossaryTerms.definition: A graduating group of trebles worked into the same chain space, typically 7 to 9 stitches wide, that forms the body of a pineapple motif. Successive rounds decrease the fan width by working into alternate tops.

content.text: grow from the magic ring, one in each diagonal direction. Rounds 3 through 5 widen then narrow each fan, with each successive round working into alternate treble tops to decrease the fan by two stitches. The outer two rounds close the motif into a square.

Use fine cotton thread and a 2.5 mm hook for the classic thread-crochet scale. In DK yarn on a 4 mm hook the pineapple reads at 15 cm across — still useful but the detail is less precise. Block the finished motif firmly with all pineapple points pinned open.

attrs.title: Materials for one motif
attrs.body: About 10 g of 4-ply cotton thread. A 2.5 mm hook. Blocking mat and pins essential.

content.text: Round 1: magic ring. *Ch 4, 1 tr, ch 1, 1 tr into ring.* Rep 3 times. Ch 4. Sl st to join. (Sets 4 diagonal pineapple base spaces.)
Round 2: into each ch-4 base sp, work (ch 3, 1 tr) 4 times. Ch 3. (Ladder of tr tops forms the pineapple base.)
Round 3: 7 tr into the large ch-sp between each pineapple base. Ch 3 between fans. (7-stitch fans.)
Round 4: *dc between tr 1 and 2, ch 3, dc between tr 3 and 4, ch 3, dc between tr 5 and 6; ch 5* across each fan. (Fans narrow.)
Round 5: work 5 tr into each ch-5 sp (fan tips). Round 6: dc across, working corners with ch 2. Round 7: granny-style corner cluster border. Fasten off.
The bruges lace tile uses a similar thread-crochet scale for geometric strip construction. Or try the filet crochet motif for another thread-based technique.
